title: One step at a time
summary: Trace a program line by line and record the values it leaves behind.

scenario.briefing: A receipt program adds two prices. The register is slow, so you must follow the values yourself and predict the final receipt total.

objectives.description: Trace the watched values to the final line.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Start with total 0 and price 4. Advance one line at a time.
Line 3 adds the current price to total.
After line 3 total is 4. Then price becomes 7, and line 5 adds it again.
Advance through every line. Final values: total 11, price 7.

misconceptions.description: Using the reassigned price in the earlier addition.
misconceptions.feedback: At line 3 the price is still 4. The assignment price = 7 happens later, so the first addition uses 4 and the total ends at 11.

misconceptions.description: Believing the assignment line itself adds to total.
misconceptions.feedback: price = 7 changes price only. total changes on the addition lines.

misconceptions.description: Believing a line can read a value assigned later in the program.
misconceptions.feedback: Execution is ordered. A line can read only values that already exist when it runs, not values assigned on later lines.

sections.title: Tracing is controlled reading
sections.body: To trace a program, keep a table of each variable and update it one line at a time. Do not jump ahead or use a value before the line that assigns it. Tracing turns code into a sequence of observable state changes.

sections.title: State changes have causes
sections.body: When a value changes, you should be able to point to the exact instruction responsible. Debugging and reviewing code depend on this skill. A stack trace or console log is useful only if you can connect it to the state that produced it.

vocabulary.definition: A line-by-line record of execution and state.
A value being followed during a trace.
The state after a particular line runs.

hints: Advance line by line and record total and price after each change.
An assignment takes effect only after its line runs; earlier lines cannot see later values.
If x starts at 1, then y = x, then x = 9, y stays 1 because the copy happened before the change.
The first addition sees price 4; only the second addition sees 7. Submit both final values.
steps.title: Trace the receipt
steps.prompt: Advance through the program, watching total and price. Then enter both final values.

snapshots.note: price changes but total does not.

steps.explanation: total becomes 4, then 11. The final value of price is 7 because it was not changed again.

steps.title: Which line changes total?
steps.prompt: In the receipt program, which line first makes total different from zero?

quiz.explanation: The addition assigns 4 to total. The previous lines only initialize values.

hints: Find the first line whose execution changes total.
Initialization sets a starting value; an assignment that adds to total changes it.
total = 0 creates the cell; total = total + price computes a new value from the old one.
Look for the first addition, not the line that changes price.
Select claims that describe what a trace can and cannot prove.
A trace records the order of state changes; it does not prove compilation correctness or future values.
A snapshot after each line shows that a value must exist before it can be read.
Two statements describe tracing accurately; reject the claims about later lines and compiler guarantees.
steps.title: What tracing proves

statements.label: A trace records how state changes over time.
A line can use a value assigned on a later line.
Every changed value should have an instruction that caused it.
If code compiles, its runtime values are automatically correct.

steps.explanation: Tracing follows the actual order of assignment. Compilation does not prove runtime correctness.

accessibility.summary: The trace can be advanced with a button and each line and watched value is plain text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Next line to advance and Tab to the final value fields.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each step announces the executed line and the current total and price.
